guard: The emitted module is closed over the seam, routes each law through it, and carries the binding-depth rule the walker keeps at run time. (FAIL-FAST suite: markers are upstream of the cells they guard.)

mutations.name: the context parameter takes a fixed name, so a program that declares it shadows the seam
mutations.find: return { ctx: free("__ctx"), temp: prefix("__t"), label: prefix("__l") };
mutations.replace: return { ctx: "__ctx", temp: prefix("__t"), label: prefix("__l") };
mutations.expectRed: a program that declares `__ctx` does not get the context's name
mutations.completionMarker: ok transform is a pure function of its source, byte for byte
mutations.cell: a program that declares `__ctx` does not get the context's name
mutations.note: The validator ADMITS a program-declared `__ctx` (measured at 9dc154f8), so a fixed name is not a naming preference: the program's binding shadows the endowment for the rest of its scope and every seam call in that region reaches a program value.

mutations.name: the cell rule never fires, so a binding written from a deeper function stays native
mutations.expectRed: a mutable binding written from a nested function is a born cell
mutations.completionMarker: ok a for-of is one iter
mutations.cell: a mutable binding written from a nested function is a born cell
mutations.note: L2032's binding half. Native bindings carry no depth, so without the cell the write from inside a concurrent branch is not refused anywhere - the shape scopes.smoke's fixture proves the validator cannot see.

mutations.name: the cell is marked and then emitted as a plain binding
mutations.expectRed: a mutable binding written from a nested function is a born cell
mutations.completionMarker: ok a for-of is one iter
mutations.cell: a mutable binding written from a nested function is a born cell
mutations.note: The analysis marking a cell and the emitter honouring it are two steps, and only the second one produces code. This is the half that would leave the mark correct and the emission native.

mutations.name: an object literal's keys are emitted verbatim, so `__proto__` can reach a prototype again
mutations.expectRed: an object literal's keys are emitted computed
mutations.completionMarker: ok a const captured by a nested function is not a cell
mutations.cell: an object literal's keys are emitted computed
mutations.note: A literal `__proto__:` key sets a prototype in JavaScript and names an own field in this language. The validator refuses that spelling today (L1028, measured); the computed form means the emitted code cannot express the hazard whatever the validator does later.

mutations.name: a member read is emitted as a native index, so it reaches the host prototype
mutations.expectRed: a member read is one get
mutations.completionMarker: ok and every surfaced member carries its reason
mutations.cell: a member read is one get
mutations.note: The member law (L4014, L4020, the curated tables, no prototype reach) is the host's, and a native index is exactly the read the walker refuses to perform.

mutations.name: a `while` header stops charging fuel, so a pure loop cannot be bounded or cancelled
mutations.completionMarker: ok and every surfaced member carries its reason
mutations.note: The step check is the only cancellation point the engine has: no wall-clock timeout, no terminate. A loop that charges nothing is a run nothing can stop.

mutations.name: `undefined` is emitted as the global name, so the module is no longer closed
mutations.expectRed: the emitted module has no unbound reference: the undefined value
mutations.completionMarker: ok and reaches no seam member outside the ruling: empty statement
mutations.cell: the emitted module has no unbound reference: the undefined value
mutations.note: Seam ruling 1: the host evaluates the module with ZERO endowments. `undefined` is a global binding, so spelling it is an unbound reference - one the compartment happens to satisfy today, which is why only a resolver over the emitted code can see it.

mutations.name: a declaring identifier is not recorded, so the emitter cannot resolve a name it declared
mutations.find: this.bindingOf.set(node, this.declare(scope, node.name as string, kind));
mutations.expectRed: resolves to nothing, which a validated program cannot contain
mutations.completionMarker: ok the emitted module has no unbound reference: array and object literals
mutations.cell: the emitted module has no unbound reference: for with per-iteration closures
mutations.note: GRADED ON THE REFUSAL, not on a cell, and deliberately: the emitter asks the analysis the same question at a declaration as at a use, and an unrecorded declaration makes a per-iteration `for` head unresolvable. It fails LOUD (the emitter refuses to emit) rather than quietly emitting a plain binding for a cell, which is the outcome worth pinning - the quiet half is covered by the mutation above.

mutations.name: an update's operand loses its numeric fast path, so every counter crosses the seam
mutations.expectRed: an update's fast path keeps a numeric counter native
mutations.completionMarker: ok an object literal's keys are emitted computed
mutations.cell: an update's fast path keeps a numeric counter native
mutations.note: `n++` is the hot path of every counted loop in the language. Without the fast path each increment is a host call, and the numeric corpus stops being the part of the differential that is identical for free.

mutations.name: an update's slow leg is emitted natively, so a non-number operand is coerced instead of refused
mutations.expectRed: an update's operand charges the coercion law when it is not a number
mutations.completionMarker: ok an update's fast path keeps a numeric counter native
mutations.cell: an update's operand charges the coercion law when it is not a number
mutations.note: The mirror of the mutation above, and it keeps the `typeof` test in place on purpose so the fast-path cell still passes and this one is what reds. Ruling 1c gave `update` the L4018 refusal; a native else branch silently answers NaN, which is the walker behaviour the ruling declined to rebuild (issue 646).

mutations.name: every unary operator is emitted natively, so `-record` stops refusing
mutations.expectRed: a unary operator that can refuse still charges it
mutations.completionMarker: ok an object literal's keys are emitted computed
mutations.cell: a unary operator that can refuse still charges it
mutations.note: The mirror of the mutation above. `-o` on a record is L4018 in the walker and NaN in native JavaScript, so the fast path may only cover what it has already proved is a number.

mutations.name: a race ships no branch bodies, so the engine cannot digest its losers
mutations.expectRed: every branch travels, because which one loses is the run's answer
mutations.completionMarker: ok a race call site ships exactly one branch payload
mutations.cell: every branch travels, because which one loses is the run's answer
mutations.note: The engine has no AST at run time, so a branch that does not travel is one the host can only digest as null - a settled race would journal a branchDigest the walker never wrote.

mutations.name: a race ships a derived form of each branch instead of the body the walker hashes
mutations.expectRed: the shipped payload digests as the walker's value over every loser set
mutations.completionMarker: ok every branch travels, because which one loses is the run's answer
mutations.cell: the shipped payload digests as the walker's value over every loser set
mutations.note: The keys still all travel, so the cell above stays green: this is the half that survives a shape check. The walker hashes ONE array of [loserName, body] pairs over a loser set only the run knows, so any per-branch derivation makes the host hash a hash and write a different byte string into a journal entry that has to be identical.

mutations.name: a call on a value is emitted natively, so a non-function callee is a host TypeError
mutations.expectRed: a call on a value charges the callee law
mutations.completionMarker: ok a for-of is one iter
mutations.cell: a call on a value charges the callee law
mutations.note: `const f = 1; f()` is admitted by the validator (measured at 9dc154f8). The walker answers L4011, a refusal the program can catch; a native call answers a host TypeError, which is a different class entirely.

mutations.name: an optional call is emitted without the flag, so the host resolves a name it should not
mutations.expectRed: a tail optional call is emitted through the ruled flag
mutations.completionMarker: ok every program the seam cannot yet express refuses loudly, and is listed
mutations.cell: a tail optional call is emitted through the ruled flag
mutations.note: Ruling 1d's flag is what makes `o.z?.()` short-circuit to undefined with nothing called. Without it the host resolves the method name unconditionally and refuses, where the walker answers undefined.

mutations.name: every method call carries the optional flag, so a missing method stops refusing
mutations.expectRed: an ordinary method call carries no flag
mutations.completionMarker: ok a tail optional call is emitted through the ruled flag
mutations.cell: an ordinary method call carries no flag
mutations.note: The mirror. `xs.nope()` is L4020 on the walker; flagged optional it would quietly answer undefined, which turns a refusal into a value the program carries on with.

mutations.name: an optional call with a chain after it is emitted instead of refused
mutations.expectRed: every program the seam cannot yet express refuses loudly, and is listed
mutations.completionMarker: ok an object literal's keys are emitted computed
mutations.cell: every program the seam cannot yet express refuses loudly, and is listed
mutations.note: The host makes the short-circuit decision and cannot tell the transform it made one. Measured on the walker: `o.z?.().x` on an absent member is undefined, `o.m?.().x` on a member returning undefined is L4010 - so emitting the continuation would answer undefined for both and silently drop a refusal.
